extracted.intended_audience: newspaper and broadcast publishers, editors, and media executives
extracted.subtask_description: Principles for running newspapers and media companies that reconcile editorial independence with business/financial imperatives; guidance aimed at managers on how to sustain high-quality journalism while meeting fiduciary and competitive demands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earn an adequate rate of return
rubrics_metrics.description: Because most news organizations are publicly held and publicly traded, they have a fiduciary responsibility to shareholders and therefore must earn an adequate rate of return.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is framed as a fact rather than a preference: unless a paper is owned by an enormously wealthy person who doesn't care about returns, profitability is a 'must do' not optional. Managers should accept this constraint when making decisions about the news operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be compelling to readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers choose what to read; newspapers must be sufficiently interesting and compelling to attract and retain audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because readership is voluntary in a competitive marketplace, finding ways to be interesting and compelling is essential. Failure to do so risks ceasing to exist as an independent enterprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do both: high-quality journalism and a successful business
rubrics_metrics.description: The choice is not between high-quality independent journalism or business success; a news organization must achieve both simultaneously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author argues this is not a trade-off — superior journalism makes the business more successful. Management should therefore seek strategies that enhance journalism as a route to long-term business vitality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honor the line between business and editorial
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a clear separation ('the line rather than the wall') so that editorial judgments are made by editors, not business staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete rule: when there's a different point of view, the editorial decision-maker wins every time. This preserves editorial independence while allowing appropriate communication between sides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make a visible cultural commitment to journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Reinforce the organization's commitment to journalism through visible symbols and rituals (e.g., displaying Pulitzer Prize winners, celebrating journalists at meetings, Journalist of the Year awards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small symbolic acts (removing unrelated artwork, displaying awards) and institutional practices (always discussing journalism at board/management/annual meetings) communicate priorities and help align the organization around journalistic values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invest in journalism despite short-term pressures
rubrics_metrics.description: Continue to invest in the news operation even when short-term financial pressures (e.g., higher newsprint costs) reduce profits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept short-term divergence (lower stock price, temporary profit decline) for the sake of long-term vitality. Management should be prepared to 'stay the course' because long-term strength depends on sustained investment in journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnose and fix non-core businesses and cost structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify when financial bleeding is caused by being in the wrong businesses or having an unsuited cost structure, and correct those issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical management action: exit businesses that don't fit the core newspaper model and adjust cost structures to what the business can support; this reduces avoidable financial strain and preserves resources for journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attract advertisers by delivering compelling journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Because advertisers largely pay the bills for many newspapers, the product must be compelling to readers to attract advertising revenue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This links editorial quality to commercial success: making the paper more compelling to readers is a direct way to maintain advertiser interest and thus financial underpinning of the enterprise.
